newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt says to reform its legal service.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt says to reform its legal service.

text.p: The Australian government's legal service will be opened to competition, cutting legal costs, Attorney-General Daryl Williams said on Monday.
Williams said the Attorney-General's Legal Practice's monopoly on Commonwealth court litigation would be progressively opened to competition until fully open from July 1, 1998.
Under the reforms, which stem from a review of the legal service, the Legal Practice would be restructured as a statutory authority separate from the minister's department.
But the minister would still control the authority, to be re-named the Australian Government Solictor (AGS).

"As a result of the restructure, the Australian Government Solicitor will have the flexibility to meet the challenge of greater contestability and competitive neutrality on the same footing as private law firms," Williams said in a statement.
"The increased competition should enable the Commonwealth to make further savings in legal costs."

Cabinet, national security and constitutional issues would remain with the AGS, but the minister could decide where to place legal work for other matters of strategic importance, advised by a new Office of Legal Services Coordination, he said. Williams did not say when legislation would be tabled in parliament to implement the reforms.
